advances: Proves the Weak Oertel bound, at an original mixed-integer point and for the original mixed volume and continuous dimension, whenever the positive-volume integer bases lie on at most \(2^{n-1}\) parallel primitive lattice lines. The bound requires neither small Hellinger gain nor a heavy individual fiber, log-affine weights, separability of the complete ambient table, or compatibility between different line profiles. It supplies the geometric antecedent of the conditional slice transfer in accepted fact `ab57fac07c0d3160` by applying the arbitrary-shape actual-body conclusion of accepted fact `5437580ffde107c8` in integer dimension one. The latter fact does not already state an unconditional theorem for this ambient line-support class. No decomposition of every positive support into this many parallel lines is asserted, and this is not the full locked target.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The one-dimensional actual-body depth theorem is used through accepted fact `5437580ffde107c8`, the actual-slice transfer and rank-zero centroid bound through accepted fact `ab57fac07c0d3160`, and global log-concavity of the complete actual volume profile through accepted fact `b563a1eb51a20cd2`. The primitive affine chart, full-dimensionality of the rank-one slice, mass normalization, and all point and volume transfers are justified above.
proof:
If \(W=0\), choose any \(\mathbf y^\star\in S\). Every containing-halfspace volume is nonnegative, so the asserted inequality holds. No table is normalized and no centroid or positive support is needed in this case. Assume henceforth that \(W>0\).

We first justify the complete lattice chart, including its saturation. Integer row operations consisting of coordinate swaps, sign changes, and addition of an integer multiple of one coordinate to another are unimodular. The Euclidean algorithm applied to the coordinates of the primitive vector \(\mathbf v\) produces a matrix \(\mathbf U\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb Z)\) with \(\mathbf U\mathbf v=\mathbf e_n\). For \(n=1\), this simply uses \(\mathbf U=1\) or \(-1\).

Every line meeting \(D\) contains some integer point \(\mathbf z_0\) and is \(\mathbf z_0+\mathbb R\mathbf v\). Its complete intersection with the lattice is \(\mathbf z_0+\mathbb Z\mathbf v\). Indeed, Bézout's identity gives integers \(a_i\) with \(\sum_i a_i v_i=1\); if \(t\mathbf v\) has integer coordinates, then \(t=\sum_i a_i(tv_i)\) is an integer. Consequently \(\mathbb R\mathbf v\cap\mathbb Z^n=\mathbb Z\mathbf v\). This direction lattice is saturated: if a nonzero integer multiple of an integer vector lies in it, that vector lies in \(\mathbb R\mathbf v\cap\mathbb Z^n\) as well. The affine chart \(t\mapsto\mathbf z_0+t\mathbf v\) therefore uses the entire intersection lattice, not the subgroup generated by selected support differences. Under \(\mathbf U\), each such line has the form \(\{b\}\times\mathbb R\), with \(b\in\mathbb Z^{n-1}\), and its integer points are exactly \(\{b\}\times\mathbb Z\). Distinct parallel lines have distinct outer indices \(b\).

Let \(\mathscr T(\mathbf x,\mathbf u)=(\mathbf U\mathbf x,\mathbf u)\), \(\widetilde C=\mathscr T(C)\), and \(\widetilde S=\mathscr T(S)=\widetilde C\cap\Lambda\). These are the chart and image notation of accepted fact `5437580ffde107c8`, specialized to zero integer translation and zero continuous shear and translation. At every integer base, \(\widetilde C_{\mathbf U\mathbf z}=C_{\mathbf z}\) and \(\widetilde w_{\mathbf U\mathbf z}=w_{\mathbf z}\), so \(\widetilde W=W\). The continuous coordinates are unchanged. Thus the map preserves every \(d\)-dimensional fiber volume, including zero volumes, and reindexes the fibers bijectively. Compactness of the base projection implies that only finitely many integer fibers are nonempty. In particular, for every ambient halfspace \(H\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)
&=\sum_{\mathbf z\in\mathbb Z^n}
\mathcal L^d\{\mathbf u\in C_{\mathbf z}:(\mathbf z,\mathbf u)\in H\}\\
&=\mathcal H_d(\widetilde S\cap\mathscr T(H)).
\end{aligned}
\]

Since \(\mathscr T\) is an invertible affine map, it takes closed halfspaces bijectively to closed halfspaces. It follows that \(h_S(\mathbf y)=h_{\widetilde S}(\mathscr T(\mathbf y))\) at every \(\mathbf y\in S\). There is no ambient determinant factor in this identity; the measure is the sum of the unchanged vertical volumes, not ambient \((n+d)\)-dimensional volume.

Write the transformed integer coordinates as \((b,t)\in\mathbb Z^{n-1}\times\mathbb Z\), and define \(w^{[b]}_t=\widetilde w_{(b,t)}\) and \(W^{[b]}=\sum_t w^{[b]}_t\). These are exactly the slice table and slice mass of accepted fact `ab57fac07c0d3160`(iv), with its \(m=n-1\), \(r=1\), and its ambient table equal to \(\widetilde w\). At most \(2^{n-1}\) outer indices have positive mass, and \(\sum_b W^{[b]}=W\). Choose one such index \(b\) of maximum mass. Then \(W^{[b]}\ge2^{-(n-1)}W>0\), and the canonical slice parameter \(\lambda=2^{n-1}W^{[b]}/W\) satisfies \(\lambda\ge1\). For \(n=1\), \(\mathbb Z^0\) consists of one empty tuple, there is one slice, and \(\lambda=1\).

Consider the actual coordinate slice

\[
C_b=\{(t,\mathbf u)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d:
(b,t,\mathbf u)\in\widetilde C\},
\qquad
\widehat S_b=C_b\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R^d).
\]

The map \(\iota_b(t,\mathbf u)=(b,t,\mathbf u)\) identifies \(\widehat S_b\) with \(S_b=\widetilde C\cap(\{b\}\times\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R^d)\), the mixed slice of accepted fact `ab57fac07c0d3160`(v). Its depth \(h_{S_b}^{\mathrm{slice}}\) is exactly \(h_{\widehat S_b}\) under \(\iota_b\), since closed relative halfspaces correspond under this affine isometry. The latter depth uses closed halfspaces in \(\mathbb R^{1+d}\) and the same \(d\)-dimensional fiber volumes. For every integer \(t\), the actual fiber \((C_b)_t\) equals \(\widetilde C_{(b,t)}\); hence the complete table of \(C_b\), including all zeros, is \(w^{[b]}\), and its mixed total is \(W^{[b]}\).

By accepted fact `b563a1eb51a20cd2`, \(\widetilde g(\mathbf x)=\mathcal L^d(\widetilde C_{\mathbf x})\), defined at every real base with zero for empty and lower-dimensional fibers, is a finite-valued globally log-concave function. Its literal restriction \(t\mapsto\widetilde g(b,t)\) is therefore globally log-concave and agrees with \(w^{[b]}_t\) at every integer \(t\). This is a restriction of the actual body, not a selection of a few positive sites or a realization by another body. Let \(A_b=\{t\in\mathbb Z:w^{[b]}_t>0\}\), exactly the positive slice support \(A_b\) in the affine-rank proof of accepted fact `ab57fac07c0d3160`. It is finite and nonempty and has affine rank either zero or one.

Suppose first that this rank is one. Choose distinct \(t_0,t_1\in A_b\). The positive-volume convex fiber at \(t_0\) contains \(d+1\) affinely independent points. Together with any point in the nonempty fiber at \(t_1\), these give \(d+2\) affinely independent points of \(C_b\). Their convex hull is a full-dimensional simplex in \(\mathbb R^{1+d}\). The slice is compact and convex because it is the pullback of \(\widetilde C\) under the affine embedding \(\iota_b\); the simplex proves that it is an actual convex body in this ambient space. This argument does not assume the positive support of the original body has full affine rank.

The affine hull of \(A_b\) is the whole real line, whose complete intersection lattice is \(\mathbb Z\). Global log-concavity gives positivity at every real point between two positive sites. Therefore \(A_b=\{a_1,\ldots,b_1\}\), where \(a_1=\min A_b\) and \(b_1=\max A_b\). At each integer midpoint it also gives \((w^{[b]}_t)^2\ge w^{[b]}_{t-1}w^{[b]}_{t+1}\); when either adjacent weight is zero this inequality is automatic. Hence the entire finite one-dimensional table satisfies the complete positive-interval and zero-table assumptions of accepted fact `5437580ffde107c8`.

Apply that fact with its integer dimension equal to one, its continuous dimension equal to the original \(d\), its actual body equal to \(C_b\), its mixed set equal to \(\widehat S_b\), and its single factor \(w^1_t=w^{[b]}_t\), positive support \(D=D_1=A_b\), and total \(W=W^{[b]}\). These are exact aliases, with no scaling of weights or volumes. Its actual-fiber witness conclusion supplies a fixed legal point \(q^\star=(t^\star,\mathbf u^\star)\in\widehat S_b\), with \(t^\star\in A_b\), for which \(h_{\widehat S_b}(q^\star)\ge(c_0/2)W^{[b]}\). There is only one factor, so no separability between different original lines is required. The theorem allows arbitrary actual fiber shapes, centroids, and translations.

If instead the rank is zero, \(A_b=\{t_0\}\) and \(\mathcal L^d((C_b)_{t_0})=W^{[b]}>0\). This single positive fiber is a compact convex body in \(\mathbb R^d\). Let \(c_{t_0}\) be its centroid and take \(q^\star=(t_0,c_{t_0})\), a legal point of \(\widehat S_b\). The centroid bound in accepted fact `ab57fac07c0d3160`(v), including its rank-zero slice justification, gives at least \(W^{[b]}/e\) in every closed continuous halfspace containing this centroid. A closed halfspace of \(\mathbb R^{1+d}\) containing \(q^\star\) restricts to such a continuous halfspace at \(t_0\), or to the entire fiber. All other integer fibers have zero volume even if nonempty. Thus \(h_{\widehat S_b}(q^\star)\ge W^{[b]}/e\ge(c_0/2)W^{[b]}\). No full-dimensional slice assumption or theorem in integer dimension zero has been used.

In either case set \(\widetilde{\mathbf y}^\star=\iota_b(q^\star)\in S_b\). The exact actual-slice transfer of accepted fact `ab57fac07c0d3160`(v) applies at this same fixed point. To spell out its geometric content, every closed ambient halfspace containing \(\widetilde{\mathbf y}^\star\) restricts on \(\{b\}\times\mathbb R^{1+d}\) to a containing closed relative halfspace or the whole affine space. Its mass in the selected slice is at least \(h_{\widehat S_b}(q^\star)\), also in the whole-space case since the slice depth is at most \(W^{[b]}\). Its full mixed mass is at least its selected-slice mass. Consequently

\[
\begin{aligned}
h_{\widetilde S}(\widetilde{\mathbf y}^\star)
&\ge h_{S_b}^{\mathrm{slice}}(\widetilde{\mathbf y}^\star)
=h_{\widehat S_b}(q^\star)\\
&\ge \frac{c_0}{2}W^{[b]}
=c_0\lambda\,2^{-n}W
\ge c_0\,2^{-n}W.
\end{aligned}
\]

Finally take \(\mathbf y^\star=\mathscr T^{-1}(\widetilde{\mathbf y}^\star)\). Its integer base is \(\mathbf U^{-1}(b,t^\star)\in\mathbb Z^n\) and its continuous coordinate is the original \(\mathbf u^\star\); in the rank-zero case use \(t^\star=t_0\), \(\mathbf u^\star=c_{t_0}\). The exact fibers and chart show \(\mathbf y^\star\in S\), in an original positive-volume fiber. Depth invariance under \(\mathscr T\) yields \(h_S(\mathbf y^\star)\ge c_0 2^{-n}W\). This one point was chosen before any containing halfspace, and the definition of depth gives the asserted simultaneous inequality for every such halfspace, including vertical halfspaces and boundary equalities.

The displayed constant is positive and satisfies \(c_0\le1/(2e)<1/e\). Throughout the proof \(d\) remains the original continuous dimension. Only an actual one-integer-coordinate slice was considered, and its mass loss is exactly compensated by \(W^{[b]}\ge2^{-(n-1)}W\). No continuous dimension was introduced, no fiber was reshaped, no volume-root dimension was changed, and no lattice-index multiplier appears. The line-count hypothesis remains a genuine additional hypothesis on the complete positive support; the proof makes no claim that every complete support satisfies it.
statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and retain the locked notation \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d\) and \(S=C\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing\). For every \(\mathbf z\in\mathbb Z^n\), define the actual fiber \(C_{\mathbf z}=\{\mathbf u\in\mathbb R^d:(\mathbf z,\mathbf u)\in C\}\), its weight \(w_{\mathbf z}=\mathcal L^d(C_{\mathbf z})\), the positive support \(D=\{\mathbf z:w_{\mathbf z}>0\}\), and \(W=\sum_{\mathbf z}w_{\mathbf z}=\mathcal H_d(S)\). Thus \(D\) is the set called \(D_+\) in the assignment, \(D\) in accepted fact `5437580ffde107c8`, and \(A\) in accepted facts `ab57fac07c0d3160` and `b563a1eb51a20cd2`; the index \(\mathbf I\) in the first fact is the present \(\mathbf z\). All these weights and totals have their original, unnormalized volume units. Empty and nonempty lower-dimensional fibers both have weight zero. The depth is the locked \(h_S(\mathbf y)=\inf_{H\ni\mathbf y}\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\), with closed ambient halfspaces \(H\).

When \(W>0\), assume there exists a primitive vector \(\mathbf v\in\mathbb Z^n\setminus\{\mathbf0\}\), meaning that its coordinates have greatest common divisor one, such that \(D\) is contained in a union of at most \(2^{n-1}\) affine lines parallel to \(\mathbb R\mathbf v\). Lines that contain no point of \(D\) may be omitted. No assumption is made about nonempty zero-volume integer fibers, or about positive real fibers at noninteger bases. When \(W=0\), impose no line hypothesis.

Use exactly the constants of accepted fact `5437580ffde107c8`, with no renormalization:

\[
\begin{aligned}
K_\ast&=64000,& M_\ast&=(16\cdot27000)^2,\\
c&=\frac{e^{-8800K_\ast}}{2(1+8M_\ast)}
\left(\frac{e^{-8}}2\right)^{M_\ast},&
c_0&=\min\left\{\frac c6,\frac1{2e}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Then \(c_0\in(0,1/e)\), and there exists \(\mathbf y^\star\in S\) such that every closed ambient halfspace \(H\) containing \(\mathbf y^\star\) satisfies \(\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\ge c_0\,2^{-n}W\). The coefficient is independent of \(n,d,C\), the line direction, the number of positive bases on a line, and all fiber shapes and translations. The conclusion includes all affine ranks of \(D\).
